title: Rigveda 3.61: To Usas
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 3.61: To Usas: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 3.61 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Usas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 3, the family book of Viśvāmitra. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 248v-249v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 3.61.1-2 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 4, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 248v
translation.original_text:
1uṣo̱ vāje̍na vājini̱ prace̍tā̱ḥ stoma̍ṁ juṣasva gṛṇa̱to ma̍ghoni | pu̱rā̱ṇī de̍vi yuva̱tiḥ pura̍ṁdhi̱r anu̍ vra̱taṁ ca̍rasi viśvavāre ||
2uṣo̍ de̱vy ama̍rtyā̱ vi bhā̍hi ca̱ndrara̍thā sū̱nṛtā̍ ī̱raya̍ntī | ā tvā̍ vahantu su̱yamā̍so̱ aśvā̱ hira̍ṇyavarṇām pṛthu̱pāja̍so̱ ye ||
translation.text:
1O Ushas, strong with strength, endowed with knowledge, accept the singer's praise, O wealthy Lady. Thou, Goddess, ancient, young, and full of wisdom, movest, all-bounteous! as the Law ordaineth.
2Shine forth, O Morning, thou auspicious Goddess, on thy bright car awaking pleasant voices. Let docile horses of far-reaching splendour convey thee hitherward, the goldencoloured.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 248v (numbered 57v by the scribe) (OPenn image 249, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.60.6 ‹-svasarāṇi yemire vratā devānām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 249r (numbered 58r by the scribe), begins in RV 3.61.3 ‹-caraṇīyamānā cakram-iva navyasi ā›. Verses 3.61.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1uṣaḥ | vājena | vājini | pra-cetāḥ | stomam | juṣasva | gṛṇataḥ | maghoni | purāṇī | devi | yuvatiḥ | puram-dhiḥ | anu | vratam | carasi | viśva-vāre
2uṣaḥ | devi | amartyā | vi | bhāhi | candra-rathā | sūnṛtāḥ | īrayantī | ā | tvā | vahantu | su-yamāsaḥ | aśvāḥ | hiraṇya-varṇām | pṛthu-pājasaḥ | ye

translation.original_ref: RV 3.61.3-6 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 4, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 249r
translation.original_text:
3uṣa̍ḥ pratī̱cī bhuva̍nāni̱ viśvo̱rdhvā ti̍ṣṭhasy a̱mṛta̍sya ke̱tuḥ | sa̱mā̱nam artha̍ṁ caraṇī̱yamā̍nā ca̱kram i̍va navya̱sy ā va̍vṛtsva ||
4ava̱ syūme̍va cinva̱tī ma̱ghony u̱ṣā yā̍ti̱ svasa̍rasya̱ patnī̍ | sva1̱̍r jana̍ntī su̱bhagā̍ su̱daṁsā̱ āntā̍d di̱vaḥ pa̍pratha̱ ā pṛ̍thi̱vyāḥ ||
5acchā̍ vo de̱vīm u̱ṣasa̍ṁ vibhā̱tīm pra vo̍ bharadhva̱ṁ nama̍sā suvṛ̱ktim | ū̱rdhvam ma̍dhu̱dhā di̱vi pājo̍ aśre̱t pra ro̍ca̱nā ru̍ruce ra̱ṇvasa̍ṁdṛk ||
6ṛ̱tāva̍rī di̱vo a̱rkair a̍bo̱dhy ā re̱vatī̱ roda̍sī ci̱tram a̍sthāt | ā̱ya̱tīm a̍gna u̱ṣasa̍ṁ vibhā̱tīṁ vā̱mam e̍ṣi̱ dravi̍ṇa̱m bhikṣa̍māṇaḥ ||
translation.text:
3Thou, Morning, turning thee to every creature, standest on high as ensign of the Immortal, To one same goal ever and ever wending now, like a wheel, O newly-born, roll hi ther.
4Letting her reins drop downward, Morning cometh, the wealthy Dame, the Lady of the dwelling; Bringing forth light, the Wonderful, the Blessed hath spread her from the bounds of earth and heaven.
5Hither invoke the radiant Goddess Morning, and bring with reverence your hymn to praise her. She, dropping sweets, hath set in heaven her brightness, and, fair to look on, hath beamed forth her splendour.
6From heaven, with hymns, the Holy One was wakened: brightly to both worlds came the wealthy Lady. To Morning, Agni, when she comes refulgent, thou goest forth soliciting fair riches.

translation.original_ref: RV 3.61.7 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 4, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 249v
translation.original_text: <sup>7</sup>ṛ̱tasya̍ bu̱dhna u̱ṣasā̍m iṣa̱ṇyan vṛṣā̍ ma̱hī roda̍sī̱ ā vi̍veśa | ma̱hī mi̱trasya̱ varu̍ṇasya mā̱yā ca̱ndreva̍ bhā̱nuṁ vi da̍dhe puru̱trā ||
translation.text: <sup>7</sup>On Law's firm base the speeder of the Mornings, the Bull, hath entered mighty earth and heaven. Great is the power of Varuṇa and Mitra, which, bright, hath spread in every place its splendour.
